**Finding submitted: deviation (WARRANTY).**

**What I found**

- **§9 "TRUELINK WARRANTIES" (p0059–p0060)** exists, but it is a pure Year 2000 date-processing warranty. There is no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no services warranty, and no stated remedy period.
- **§11 "STANDARD OF CARE" (p0069)** requires only "the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" — self-referential, unbounded in time, and with no repair/re-perform/refund remedy. It does not reach the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies).
- **§8 (p0051, p0056)** imposes compliance-with-laws and malicious-code warranties on **Client only** — the mirror obligations on TrueLink are absent.
- **Disclaimer (p0076)** is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does *not* swallow express warranties. No carve-out edit was needed — the gap is the missing warranty itself, not an over-broad disclaimer. This also means we are not in walk-away "AS IS" territory.
- Searches for "conform" and "professional and workmanlike" returned nothing anywhere in the document, confirming no unlisted section carries a vendor performance warranty.

**Redline (validated ok:true)** — inserts after p0060, into §9, at the **preferred** position: professional/workmanlike services; 12-month software conformance and 90-day services conformance; TrueLink compliance with laws; no malicious code; and repair/replacement/re-performance or refund of fees as Client's remedy. The comment offers the 90/30-day fallback as a negotiating concession.

One note recorded in the rationale rather than flagged separately: §4 (p0043) and §5 (p0045) contain unfilled blanks ("not less than ____ months", "$____ per month"), which is a separate commercial-completeness issue outside this rule.
